page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.xlarge is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 4 vCPUs across 2 dedicated physical Intel Xeon processor cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate moderate single-thread execution, scoring 1302.0 in Geekbench single-core and achieving 27.08 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core throughput remains in the lower quartile, reflecting the 2-core hardware topology with Geekbench multi-core registering 2768.0 and stress-ng multi-core recording 3790.8.

Memory bandwidth tests show 25.95 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 17.08 GB/sec for uncached write operations, while Redis SET operations sustain 3.7 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput reaches 3.93 GB/sec. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with modest multi-threaded compute density, this instance profile provides cost-efficient operation for memory-demanding applications that do not require intense parallel compute, such as caching tiers, intermediate relational databases, lightweight text analytics, and enterprise staging environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.xlarge is a memory-dense virtual machine configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.5 GHz and 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization, it provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instruction sets. The server includes no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage and offering a 2 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks place single-thread computational capacity within the average range, whereas multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth register lower results due to the two physical core constraint. This hardware balance suits memory-centric workloads with moderate CPU requirements, such as caching nodes, small in-memory databases, and memory-buffered background services.
